282	## 2026-08-23 — E-ONE-RECEIPT-MANY-BORROWED-CONSUMERS-1 — the integration half of #1012: one versioned tokenization drives Tantivy, DeepNSM-v2 and a forward surface with zero re-tokenization, and the four gaps that stand between that and a carrier
283	
284	**Status:** FINDING — [MEASURED] (`PROBE-TOKEN-SEAM-1`, 37 gates, **13
285	disable-runs each verified red-then-green**; two committed real corpora — the
286	in-tree KJV Genesis scene `PROBE-TOKEN-BPE-GEOMETRY-1` used, carried verbatim so
287	the numbers are comparable, and Project Gutenberg's *Alice* split into 300
288	paragraphs, 75 514 B). The probe lives in `AdaWorldAPI/paperless-rs`
289	(`crates/paperless-token`, `docs/TOKEN-SEAM-ARCHITECTURE.md`) because it needs a
290	Tantivy dependency this workspace does not carry; this entry records the
291	**lance-graph-side** findings.
292	**This closes the integration half** of
293	`E-TOKEN-BPE-CAN-FIT-NOT-YET-BUY-1` (#1012). That verdict measured that BPE FITS
294	the `6×(8:8)` geometry and refused to buy a carrier. It did not ask whether one
295	tokenization can SERVE several consumers at once. It can.
296	**Confidence:** High for what is measured at these two corpus scales; the 8-bit
297	lane saturated at 75 KB, so nothing here is a scale claim.
298	
299	**Headline.** ONE tokenization per span drove all three consumers and each added
300	**zero** further tokenizations — not by discipline but by construction. Totals:
301	313 source tokenizations for 308 spans plus 5 deliberate fixtures, and 1 QUERY
302	tokenization on a deliberately separate counter (a query is different bytes;
303	folding it into one number would make the claim a lie).
304	
305	**The two facts that make it adoptable, and neither was designed for this:**
306	
307	1. **DeepNSM-v2's library is already tokenizer-free.** `parse_to_spo(&[Tagged])`
308	   consumes `(WordId, Pos)` pairs and touches no string; the
309	   `split_whitespace`/`normalise` logic lives ONLY in `examples/bible_wave.rs`
310	   and `examples/genre_shapes.rs`. The seam needed **no change to the crate**.
311	   The `(WordId, Pos)` boundary is the shipped seam and nobody had used it as
312	   one.
313	2. **Tantivy structurally cannot own offsets.** Its indexer reads `Token::text`
314	   and `Token::position`, uses `position_length` transiently, and reads
315	   `offset_from`/`offset_to` NOWHERE outside its own tests. Offsets are consumed
316	   only by snippet generation, which re-tokenizes the STORED text at query time.
317	   An index cannot become the ABI here even by accident.
318	
319	**Measured, and the numbers are the point rather than the verdict:**
320	
321	| | KJV scene | Alice |
322	|---|---|---|
323	| bytes / spans / tokens | 1 126 / 8 / 354 | 75 514 / 300 / 37 149 |
324	| compression | 3.18× | **2.03×** |
325	| distinct ids used | 137 | **247 of 255** |
326	| resident lane bytes | 832 (74 % of source) | 55 572 (74 %) |
327	| receipt share of resident | 54 % | 30 % |
328	| particles/span p50/p95/max | 4 / 8 / 8 | 8 / 30 / 43 |
329	| tokens per lexical unit p50/max | 1 / 7 | 2 / 15 |
330	| tokens straddling a word boundary | 30 | 58 |
331	
332	- **The 8-bit lane SATURATES.** 247 of 255 ids on 75 KB of ordinary English, with
333	  compression already fallen from 3.18× to 2.03×. The canon's answer — the hi
334	  byte of each `(8:8)` pair as a PAGE lane, two separate bytes, never a widened
335	  `u16` — is **untested**. Until it is measured no scale claim about token BPE
336	  should be made, and this supersedes any reading of #1012's 3.35× as a
337	  corpus-independent figure.
338	- **The resident lane is ~74 % of the source text, not a fraction of it**, and
339	  at these span sizes **framing is 30–54 % of it**. A 56-byte receipt against
340	  12-byte particles means the RECEIPT's column layout matters more than the
341	  particle's. #1012 could not see this — it had no receipt.
342	- **Cardinality is not 1:1 in either direction**, so a BPE↔`WordId` projection
343	  is a real function, not a relabelling. Nothing in the seam assigns a `WordId`
344	  to a BPE token; that would be a second vocabulary wearing DeepNSM's
345	  coordinate system.
346	- **Byte offsets are DERIVED**, by prefix sum over a per-id decoded-length
347	  table. The receipt stores no offset column at all.
348	
349	**Four lance-graph-side gaps, each named rather than worked around:**
350	
351	1. **No shipped token continuation mechanism anywhere.** The nearest precedent
352	   in SHAPE is `rail_geometry::RailCarving::AxisSlab { reg, cont: Option<usize> }`,
353	   which chains one register to one continuation and caps at `RAIL_MAX_DEPTH = 24`
354	   levels — **below the measured p50 of 4 particles**, so it does not fit. The
355	   probe uses a contiguous run (`first_particle + particle_count + token_count`).
356	   Stated honestly there are TWO lawful framings and the trade is exact:
357	   `particle_count` alone bounds the run and a PAD scan inside that bound is
358	   already exact BECAUSE PAD is reserved (cost: one vocabulary slot, which at a
359	   255-cap that saturates is not free); or `token_count` costs 4 bytes and frees
360	   the slot for a full 256-id alphabet. What is unlawful is inferring the end
361	   from padding with no bound — measured, a lane-wide PAD scan overshoots
362	   receipt 0 by 10 tokens straight into receipt 1.
363	2. **`ValueTenant` has no token variant** (16 discriminants, none for text), so a
364	   lawful resident lane must implement `SoaEnvelope` or land as a new tenant.
365	   The probe's lane is a probe-local `Vec` and says so.
366	3. **There is no callable part-of-speech surface, and the reason is a decision
367	   already taken.** `coca_pos`/`archaic_pos`/`normalise` are byte-identical in
368	   BOTH deepnsm-v2 examples, above a comment stating `deepnsm_v2::lexicon` was
369	   DELETED after an audit found `lance-graph-planner`'s `insight_coca_read`
370	   already grounds it. That grounding does not reach a lean consumer:
371	   `insight_coca_read` is itself an **example binary**, in a crate carrying
372	   `serde`/`serde_yml`/`tokio`/`ndarray`, and its master `lexicon.tsv` is absent
373	   from this checkout. The probe restated the twenty-line tagger rather than
374	   re-litigate the deletion — recorded so the next consumer has the evidence the
375	   audit did not.
376	4. **The semantic half is unexercised.** `cam96_codebook.bin` / `cam96_codes.bin`
377	   are release assets, absent here, so palette256² DISTANCE never ran. Only the
378	   lexical/grammar half was measured.
379	
380	**Polars: refuted, and the honest form is weaker than the question invited.** A
381	sweep of nine checkouts found **zero** `polars` occurrences in any manifest or
382	source; every `DataFrame` mention is prose. `paperless-rs` and `tesseract-rs`
383	declare none of arrow/datafusion/lance/lancedb. There was nothing to remove. The
384	structured-evidence path is likewise not tabular algebra:
385	`lance-graph-arm-discovery` takes `Dataset { spec: FeatureSpec, rows:
386	Vec<Vec<u32>> }` — category-index rows against a schema.
387	
388	**Method note, and it is the transferable part.** An independent vacuity audit of
389	the finished probe found FIVE holes: a gate asserting byte counts but never span
390	counts (the CRLF bug that collapsed 300 spans into 1 would have re-passed it), a
391	threshold true by construction, an assertion about a type signature rather than
392	behaviour, an unconditional prefix check, and an unexercised ASCII-vs-Unicode
393	whitespace divergence. All five are fixed; four gained their own disable-runs;
394	the fifth is bounded by a measured count of 0. Separately, TWO disable-runs were
395	themselves wrong first — one relaxed a knob that does not bind on the fixture,
396	one targeted a mechanism the gate did not actually rest on — and an early batch
397	reported "no failure" six times in a row because the probe binary path was wrong
398	and nothing ran. **A knob that does not bind is not a disable; a fixture's SHAPE
399	is part of a test's coverage; and a null result is a claim about the apparatus
400	until proven otherwise.**
401	
402	**⚠ SELF-CORRECTION, same session, after being pointed at `ogar-doc-ir`.** Two
403	claims above were wrong and are corrected here rather than left standing:
404	
405	1. **The seam invented an identity that already existed.** The first cut minted
406	   `source_id`/`span_id` integers. `ogar_doc_ir::DocIr` already answers all
407	   three questions a tokenization receipt asks — `content_sha256` for WHICH
408	   document, `(DocPage::number, Region::reading_order)` for WHICH span, and
409	   `Region::text` for the span's canonical text. The probe was re-cut to read
410	   them (`docir.rs`; gates `T-DOCIR` / `T-DOCIR-KEY` / `T-DOCIR-SPANS`, 41
411	   total, 18 disable-runs). Note the crate's own docs CORRECT its plan's first
412	   sketch on what that hash is: a **per-acquisition dedup key**, not a
413	   cross-retina identity — which is exactly the right reading for a receipt,
414	   because you tokenize bytes.
415	2. **"The OCR boundary supplies no byte offsets" is RETIRED as a gap.** It
416	   supplies no PAGE-wide offset and does not need to: a region owns its text,
417	   so an offset is region-local, and `ogar-from-docv1::region_text` is where the
418	   `leading_space`-aware join already happens. What remains is far smaller — a
419	   sub-region span needs a non-zero `byte_from`, which the receipt already
420	   carries and no producer emits.
421	
422	Also corrected: the `247 of 255` figure quoted above is the count of ids
423	APPEARING in the lane, not the vocabulary size. Measured, the trained table is
424	**full at 255/255** on Alice (and on the whole 170 KB file), and **180 of 255**
425	on the KJV fixture — where, as #1016's own record of that fixture says, the
426	CORPUS rather than the cap set it. The saturation conclusion holds and is
427	stronger; the number was the wrong quantity.
428	
429	**Untouched by this.** HHTL is address geometry and BPE is tokenization —
430	#1012's measured refutation of the merge tree as a radix prefix partition
431	stands. Content never travels in classid: the contract id is a FIELD on the
432	receipt, gated by a grep of the library's own non-comment source.
